sections.heading: How a semester runs
sections.html:
Six-week courses meet once a week for three hours, in cohorts that stay together from Foundations to Finishing. Machines, mats, and irons belong to the academy; fabric lists go out two weeks before the first class, with amounts honest enough to include mistakes.

Every cohort ends with a finished quilt on the studio wall for one week, photographed for the family group chat and the academy's album alike.

sections.title: Enroll for the fall term
sections.body: Foundations cohorts start four times a year, and the waiting list moves every semester.

sections.heading: Supplies
sections.html: The academy provides machines, mats, irons, and the classroom stash of neutral thread. Students buy fabric and one good rotary blade; the supply lists say exactly how much, with the mistakes budgeted in.

items.q: I have never touched a sewing machine.
items.a: Foundations 101 assumes exactly that, and the first class is threading, seams, and not being afraid of the machine yet.
Life happens once per course: the studio reopens on Sunday afternoons for make-up sessions with an instructor present.
Fifteen for the evening cohorts. Younger stitchers do better in the Saturday family sessions, which run each semester.

sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: For alumni and current students: machine hours outside class, the library, and the good cutting tables.

sections.heading: What membership means
sections.html: Members sew at the academy any open studio hour: machines set up, irons hot, and an instructor on site for the questions that halt a project at nine at night. Membership also holds your place in cohort registration, which fills in the order the list is kept.

sections.title: The studio is open late on Thursdays
sections.body: Members sew until ten, and the kettle follows the cohort schedule.

sections.title: About the academy
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Founded in a church basement with four card tables, now a storefront studio with twelve stations that all run true.

sections.html:
The academy began when a community-ed quilting class outgrew its room three times in two years and its teacher decided the curriculum deserved a building. The piecing room still uses the same sequence taught on those card tables, refined by every cohort that has argued with a curve since.

The school's rule is written over the ironing board: nobody rips alone. Mistakes are repaired in company or not at all.

items.quote: I finished my first quilt at fifty-nine and my granddaughter's at sixty-one. The wall of finished quilts is the best advertising in the city.
items.author: A Foundations alum
